claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances and it is over tolerance. The trip record gives actual_distance_km 40.1 against optimal_distance_km 38.3, a deviation of 1.80 km, which exceeds POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is measured from those recorded distances, not re-measured from the trace, so the 1.80 km figure is the one that governs and the within-tolerance rows of POL-RD-24 are closed off.

The trace shows which route was actually driven, independent of the recorded distances. The driver-device fixes run on the Pan-Island Expressway from 23:49:57 and on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway from 00:02:27, matching the record's route_deviation_detected event at 23:50:00 at the Jurong West Avenue 2 / PIE slip road (recommended AYE, vehicle took PIE) and the route_rejoined event at the ECP / KPE interchange at 00:14:25. The booked route on the record was Jurong West Central 2, AYE, MCE, ECP, Airport Boulevard at 38.3 km — the route the rider says the app showed.

The reroute was not traffic-justified. The only traffic data in the record, EV-ADVIS-05012-01, is a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY of type NONE for the AYE segment, and its own derivation records justifies_reroute as false because NONE is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 names — closure, congestion or incident. POL-RD-23 is express that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute, so the driver's statement that 'night time PIE is faster' cannot carry the justification; it is an assertion, not data.

The driver also failed the independent duty in POL-RD-21 to inform the rider of the deviation before or at the point of deviation. The chat log for this trip is empty — message_count 0, no messages, not truncated — and the trip record carries no in-app calls. There is therefore neither a chat message nor a recorded call of the kind POL-RD-21 requires, and the rider was never told the driver was leaving the recommended AYE/MCE route.

On those facts exactly one row of POL-RD-24 applies: row (d), not traffic-justified and deviation over 1 km, which refunds the excess distance fare in full. The rider's remedy is therefore a PARTIAL_REFUND of the excess distance fare — part of the trip's charge returned to the filing party under POL-GEN-03 — and not NO_ACTION, which would leave the rider carrying a charge the deviation has displaced.

The amount of that refund is 1.66 SGD. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge: 1.80 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.656 SGD, rounded half up to 1.66 SGD, which is the figure the payments ledger itself derives. The rider notes the 40.04 SGD surge line and the 90.99 SGD total, but the POL-RD-24 formula applies no surge to the excess distance fare, and the rider asks only for the sum the matrix gives — 1.66 SGD — rather than a remedy the route-deviation policy does not provide.

No fact row (d) needs is missing, so POL-GEN-26 does not bite here. The deviation distance comes from the recorded distances and the traffic-justification question is answered by the advisory of type NONE; notification under POL-RD-21 is not an element of row (d), so the empty chat log and the absence of a call recording — which POL-RD-21 says cannot establish a purely verbal notice — leave nothing open that would force the case to be escalated instead of decided.

The contested amount, 90.99 SGD, is above POL-GEN-22's 50.00 SGD band, so the file goes to human review with the AI preparing the case; POL-RD-25 holds the AI ruling to POL-GEN-22's gate and to a confidence of 0.80. The rider asks that the reviewer take into the file the entitlement the record already establishes under POL-RD-24(d) — 1.66 SGD returned to the rider — and not leave the charge standing.

The rider asks for the whole 90.99 SGD fare back, but POL-RD-24's matrix never returns a whole trip fare: the only remedy it provides for a route deviation is the excess distance fare, and the only values it licenses are NO_ACTION, PARTIAL_REFUND and ESCALATE. The rider is therefore not 'entirely right' within POL-GEN-03 and FULL_REFUND cannot issue on this record; the metered charge stands except for, at most, its excess-distance element.

The driver's maximum exposure on this trip is 1.66 SGD: the excess distance fare is deviation_km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent, i.e. 1.80 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.66 SGD. That is under 2% of the 90.99 SGD charged on a 38.3 km journey the driver completed in 39 minutes. Any award above 1.66 SGD would be a remedy POL-RD-24 does not license.

The 90.99 SGD the rider contests is dominated by a surge of 40.04 SGD at multiplier 1.8, and the refund matrix never touches surge: the POL-RD-24 formula is applied with surge_applied false. The rider's real grievance - 'the fare was far more than I expected' - is the late-night metered surge, and no clause in this policy puts surge in play.

The deviation the record permits is 1.80 km and no more: 40.1 km recorded actual minus 38.3 km recorded optimal, the platform's recorded distances, which are the measure POL-RD-22 fixes. The GPS trace is expressly not used to re-measure the distance, so there is no basis on the trace to enlarge the deviation, and equally none to inflate any refund beyond the recorded figure.

The deviation is a single closed segment, not an open-ended detour: the trip record opens it at the Jurong West Avenue 2 / PIE slip road at 23:50:00 and closes it with route_rejoined at the ECP / KPE interchange at 00:14:25, and the trace shows the vehicle on the PIE, then the KPE, then back on the recommended ECP corridor to Airport Boulevard. The rider's loss is bounded to that segment.

The matrix refunds distance, not time. The trip ran 39.0 minutes against a 37.2 minute optimal, but POL-RD-24's formula is deviation_km x per_km_rate_sgd only, so the 9.36 SGD time fare and the roughly 0.43 SGD attributable to 1.8 extra minutes lie outside any refund this policy provides.

The driver does not claim traffic justification, and candidly cannot: the LTA record for the recommended AYE segment shows advisory type NONE with no incident, roadwork or closure, and POL-RD-23 requires data of that kind, not the driver's assertion that the PIE is faster at night. Nor does he claim he told the rider - the chat log is empty and no in-app call was placed. But neither failing enlarges the money: POL-RD-24 pays the same excess distance fare in row (b) (traffic-justified, not informed) as in row (d) (not traffic-justified), so on these recorded distances the driver's exposure stays at 1.66 SGD.

To the extent the rider's demand is a complaint about the fare itself - 'I want the whole fare refunded' - that is the fare and surge head of dispute, which POL-GEN-24 removes from AI adjudication in this version and routes to human review. It cannot produce a refund inside this route-deviation case, and no row of POL-RD-24 funds it.

The contested amount is 90.99 SGD, above POL-GEN-22's 50.00 SGD ceiling, so this case goes to human review and the AI prepares the case file only; POL-RD-25 withdraws the AI ruling for the same reason. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalated case holds the amount and issues no monetary outcome, so the metered fare stands and nothing is refunded to the rider now, while the driver's position - that the rider's exposure is capped at the 1.66 SGD excess distance fare - is preserved for the reviewer.
